boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Elmhurst University traditions, recurring ceremonies and school-specific rituals, from Bluejay Homecoming customs to long-running musical gatherings.

cards.title: Watch the Bluejays Circle Campus
cards.subtitle: The Homecoming Parade along Prospect Avenue
cards.notes: Claim a public viewing spot near Prospect Avenue and watch student groups, spirit teams and alumni entries circle the Elmhurst campus.
cards.short_summary: A campus-edge procession turns Prospect Avenue into Elmhurst’s annual Bluejay reunion route.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University reports that its 2025 Homecoming Parade traveled on streets surrounding campus and included 22 participating groups; its institutional history dates the first Homecoming to 1923.
cards.access_notes: The cited recap documents the 2025 parade; consult the current Homecoming schedule before attending a future edition.

cards.title: Turn a Club Banner into Homecoming History
cards.subtitle: Student-made banners displayed in Founders Lounge
cards.notes: During Homecoming Week, stop in Founders Lounge to compare the student organizations’ themed banners and spot the competition winners.
cards.short_summary: Campus groups translate each Homecoming theme into hand-decorated banners displayed together indoors.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University documented more than 30 clubs, residence halls and organizations entering its 2023 Homecoming Student Banner Competition, with their banners displayed in Founders Lounge.
cards.source_title: Homecoming 2023: Once a Great Time, Always a Great Time
cards.access_notes: Participation and public viewing arrangements vary; verify the current Homecoming program and Frick Center access.

cards.title: Follow the Homecoming Clues
cards.subtitle: Elmhurst’s annual campus medallion search
cards.notes: Join only through the published Homecoming instructions, follow official clues and keep the search to spaces where participants are permitted.
cards.short_summary: A hidden medallion gives Elmhurst students a school-specific Homecoming puzzle to solve.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University’s 2020 Homecoming recap identifies the Medallion Hunt as an annual student activity held during Homecoming Week.
cards.source_title: Elmhurst U. Celebrates a Historic Homecoming 2020
cards.access_notes: The direct source documents the 2020 hunt; confirm that it appears in the current student Homecoming schedule before participating.

cards.title: Hear the Hash Bell Open Homecoming Service
cards.subtitle: A historic bell ritual at Elmhurst’s Sunday service
cards.notes: If the service returns to the schedule, listen for the opening bell and use the ceremony to connect Homecoming with Elmhurst’s history.
cards.short_summary: Elmhurst’s traditional Homecoming Sunday service has opened with the ringing of its distinctively named hash bell.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University states that its traditional 2020 Homecoming Sunday Service opened with University Chaplain H. Scott Matheney ringing the hash bell.
cards.source_title: Elmhurst U. Celebrates a Historic Homecoming 2020
cards.access_notes: This ritual is directly documented for 2020; its continuation is unverified, so check the current Homecoming schedule.

cards.entity_name: Elmhurst University Festival of Lessons & Carols
cards.title: Count Nine Readings by Candle-Season Light
cards.subtitle: Elmhurst’s Advent-to-Christmastide choral tradition
cards.notes: Choose one announced service, arrive before doors open and follow nine readings accompanied by performances from University choirs.
cards.short_summary: Scripture and Elmhurst choral music alternate in a seasonal campus ceremony established generations ago.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University calls the Festival of Lessons & Carols an annual University tradition, held at Elmhurst since 1961 and structured around nine Scriptural readings with choir music.
cards.source_title: Festival of Lessons & Carols to be Held on Dec. 5
cards.access_notes: The cited 2025 services were open to all; check the University calendar for the next date, format and entry details.

cards.title: Hear College Bands Face the Festival Stage
cards.subtitle: A multi-day Elmhurst jazz and education tradition
cards.notes: Pick a college-band session or featured concert, then listen for the guest artists’ critiques that distinguish the festival format.
cards.short_summary: Visiting college ensembles perform for prominent jazz artists before Elmhurst’s featured concerts.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University documented the 56th annual Jazz Festival in 2023 as a four-day event where college and university bands performed for guest jazz artists who provided critiques and honors.
cards.source_title: 56th Annual Elmhurst University Jazz Festival Begins Feb. 23
cards.access_notes: Sessions may be offered in person or by livestream; consult the current festival program for tickets and venue access.

cards.title: Bring a Blanket for Elmhurst’s Summer Soundtrack
cards.subtitle: The annual outdoor concert on the University Mall
cards.notes: Pack a lawn chair or blanket for the University Mall and check the forecast and event page before joining this outdoor concert.
cards.short_summary: Elmhurst welcomes summer with its Jazz Band, visiting artists and a picnic-style audience on the Mall.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University presented June Jazz 2025 as its 29th annual concert, an outdoor University Mall performance featuring guest artists with the Elmhurst University Jazz Band.
cards.access_notes: The cited 2025 event was free and public; verify the next concert’s date, weather plan and entry terms.

cards.entity_name: Town vs. Gown Vintage Baseball Game
cards.title: Cheer Like an 1850s Baseball “Krank”
cards.subtitle: Elmhurst University versus the City under vintage rules
cards.notes: Bring a chair to the Mall, learn the period baseball vocabulary and cheer for either the University or City team from the sidelines.
cards.short_summary: University and City squads turn the Mall into an old-rule ballfield complete with nineteenth-century slang.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University describes its recurring Vintage Baseball Game as a Town vs. Gown matchup between City and University teams, played on the Mall using rules and terminology from the 1850s.
cards.source_title: Vintage Baseball Game Returns to Elmhurst University on June 4
cards.access_notes: The cited 2023 game was free and public; verify the next edition’s date and spectator guidance before visiting.

cards.title: Open an Acceptance with the Bluejay Crew
cards.subtitle: A surprise welcome for selected admitted students
cards.notes: If selected for a visit, follow the admission team’s directions and capture the moment with the Bluejay Box and welcoming crew.
cards.short_summary: Elmhurst takes selected acceptance celebrations on the road with boxes, school gear and Victor E. Bluejay.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University identified presidential visits to selected newly admitted students and presentation of Bluejay Box welcome gifts as an annual tradition in 2020.
cards.source_title: Newly Admitted Students Get a Special Delivery
cards.access_notes: This is an invitation-based admission activity for selected students, not a drop-in campus event; current continuation is unverified.

cards.title: Applaud Elmhurst’s Service Traditions
cards.subtitle: Annual recognition of campus leadership and service
cards.notes: Attend through the published invitation or event details and listen for the Founders, Senior of the Year and Bluejay honors.
cards.short_summary: Elmhurst closes the leadership year by recognizing service, involvement and Bluejay spirit in a named awards ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University describes the Student Leadership Awards as an annual event and reports that its 2026 ceremony presented Founders Awards, Senior of the Year and the Dr. Phil Riordan Bluejay of the Year Award.
cards.source_title: Five Students Win Top Achievement Awards
cards.access_notes: Attendance eligibility is not stated on the cited page; consult Student Affairs for current ceremony access.
